def is_plain_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a single file name with no path separators or dot-dot parts."""
    ex is_plain_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_plain_name("../secret.txt") == False
    ex is_plain_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_plain_name("notes/../../secret.txt") == False
    ex is_plain_name("") == False
    return name.char_count() > 0 and "/" not in name and "\\" not in name and ".." not in name

def read_note(name: str) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the file `name` inside the directory `notes`.

    `name` is untrusted. Only files inside `notes` are read, and no name,
    including absolute paths or ones containing `..`, may reach a file
    outside `notes`. A missing or unreadable file gives "".
    """
    if not is_plain_name(name):
        return ""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        return fs.read_text(name) else ""
